question: How are the many womb-cavities within maya illustrated by analogy?
premises: Many inner rooms can be enclosed within one hall.
The womb-cavities are similarly enclosed within one head-hall of maya.
The verse uses a direct analogy to explain their arrangement.
inference: The multiplicity of womb-cavities exists within a single encompassing structure of maya, like rooms within one hall.
uncertainties: The term māyāśiraḥsāle is unusual and may be a technical cosmological expression.
plain_english: Just as many inner rooms are enclosed within one hall, so the womb-cavities are enclosed within the one head-hall of maya.
